name: Jetheth
overview: Jetheth was a male Edomite who held the position of chief of Edom, as recorded in Genesis 36:40. His leadership role indicates a significant status within the Edomite tribe, descendants of Esau. Beyond his chiefdom, there are no additional notes or details about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: Jetheth is the only recorded name for this individual, appearing in Genesis 36:40. There is no provided meaning or special significance attached to his name in the scriptural text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Jetheth as a descendant of Esau, linking him to the Edomite lineage. No other family relationships are recorded for Jetheth beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jetheth's importance in the biblical narrative stems from his role as a chief of Edom, reflecting the established leadership structure among Esau's descendants. His mention in Genesis 36:40 places him within the genealogical and tribal history that outlines the heritage of Edom. This record contributes to the broader understanding of the nations and peoples related to Israel's family line.
